# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".

  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
OutOfBoundaryRule::validate
Summary: Ensures that both the source and destination squares of a move
         lie inside the playing board (0 <= x, y < size). Moves that
         reach outside the board are rejected.
Algorithm:
  1. size = game.getConfiguration().size.
  2. For each of move.source and move.destination:
       - Require 0 <= x < size and 0 <= y < size.
  3. If both squares are in bounds, return true; otherwise return false.
Related Features: configuration.size (board side length, must be odd
                  per the Initialization requirement, but this rule
                  only checks the bounds, not the parity).
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Move, Place
Input:
  - game : Game - used to read the board size.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose endpoints are checked.
Output:
  - boolean - true if both squares lie inside the board; false
              otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - configuration has been loaded and exposes a positive odd size.
Post-condition:
  - No mutation.

  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
KnightBlockRule::validate
Summary: Implements the "horse leg" blocking rule from Chinese chess:
         when a Knight moves two squares in one direction and one
         square in the perpendicular direction, the square immediately
         adjacent to the source in the primary direction is called the
         "blocking" (or "hobbling") square. If any piece occupies that
         blocking square, the move is illegal.
Algorithm:
  1. src = move.source, dst = move.destination.
  2. Compute the absolute differences: |dx| = |dst.x - src.x|,
     |dy| = |dst.y - src.y|.
  3. If the move is not an L-shape ((|dx|,|dy|) is not (1,2) or (2,1)),
     this rule does not apply; return true (let KnightMoveRule, if
     evaluated, decide shape validity).
  4. Determine the primary direction (the one with step 2):
       - If |dx| == 2 (primary is horizontal): blocking square is
         ((src.x + dst.x) / 2, src.y).
       - If |dy| == 2 (primary is vertical):   blocking square is
         (src.x, (src.y + dst.y) / 2).
  5. If game.getPiece(blocking) != null, return false.
  6. Otherwise return true.
Related Features: KnightBlockRule has no fields.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - game : Game - used to inspect the blocking square.
  - move  : Move - the candidate Knight move being validated.
Output:
  - boolean - true if the blocking square is empty (or the move is not
              an L-shape); false if a piece blocks the Knight's leg.
Pre-condition:
  - KnightMoveRule (or equivalent shape check) has confirmed the move
    is L-shaped, or the caller will not rely on this rule for
    non-L-shaped moves.
Post-condition:
  - No mutation of the game state.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

   invalid initialization parameters.

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
KnightMoveRule::validate
Summary: Validates that a proposed move is a legal L-shaped Knight move:
         the source and destination must differ by exactly (2,1) or
         (1,2) in absolute coordinates, and the destination must be
         inside the board. The "horse leg" blocking check is handled
         separately by KnightBlockRule.
Algorithm:
  1. src = move.source, dst = move.destination.
  2. Compute |dx| = |dst.x - src.x|, |dy| = |dst.y - src.y|.
  3. If (|dx|, |dy|) is one of {(1,2), (2,1)}, return true.
  4. Otherwise return false.
Related Features: KnightMoveRule has no fields.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state (available for symmetry with
                  other rules; not strictly required for an L-shape
                  check).
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source/destination geometry
                    is checked.
Output:
  - boolean - true if the move is an L-shape with offsets 1 and 2;
              false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - The caller has already verified the source is non-null and
    in-bounds via the global rule pipeline.
Post-condition:
  - No side effects.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::start
Summary: Drives the main game loop for a JesonMor match. It alternates
         turns between the registered players, fetches each player's
         legal moves, asks the player to pick one, executes it, updates
         the score, refreshes the console, and checks for a winner. The
         loop terminates when a winner is determined or when a player
         has no available moves.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize the board from configuration.initialBoard.
  2. Set currentPlayer = configuration.players.get(0).
  3. Loop:
       a. available = this.getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer).
       b. If available is empty:
            - winner = this.getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove)
              using the no-moves / score-tiebreak path.
            - Return winner.
       c. chosen = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, available).
       d. lastPiece  = this.getPiece(chosen.source).
       e. lastMove   = chosen.
       f. this.movePiece(chosen).
       g. this.updateScore(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
       h. this.refreshOutput().
       i. winner = this.getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
          If winner != null, return winner.
       j. Advance currentPlayer to the other player in
          configuration.players (two-player rotation).
  4. (Unreachable in normal play; the loop only exits via return.)
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer, configuration,
                  configuration.players, Player.score.
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Player, Move, Place, Piece,
                 Knight, Archer, ConsolePlayer, RandomPlayer
Input:
  - None (operates entirely on the receiver's configuration field).
Output:
  - Player - the winner of the game once the loop terminates.
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is non-null and has at least two players.
  - The board size is odd, and initial placements are within bounds.
  - configuration.numMovesProtection is non-negative.
  - The Configuration has been validated (else InvalidConfigurationError
    may be thrown during initialization).
Post-condition:
  - The returned Player is one of the players in configuration.players.
  - The board reflects the last executed move.
  - Scores reflect all successfully executed moves.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a previously validated move on the board by relocating
         the piece from the move's source square to its destination
         square and clearing the source. The board representation is
         updated in place; this method assumes the move has already
         passed the rule pipeline.
Algorithm:
  1. piece = this.getPiece(move.source).
  2. this.setPiece(move.destination, piece)   // place piece at dst.
  3. this.setPiece(move.source, null)         // vacate the source.
  4. (Optionally) increment game.numMoves to record the executed turn.
     (In the standard loop, the caller / updateScore is responsible for
      this, but the JesonMor implementation increments it here as part
      of movePiece so that FirstNMovesProtectionRule sees the right
      counter on the next validation pass.)
Related Features: board (mutated), numMoves (incremented), currentPlayer
                  (unchanged here, but conceptually the mover).
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - move : Move - the move to execute. Must be a fully legal move
                  (already passed all rules).
Output:
  - void
Pre-condition:
  - move.source and move.destination are both in-bounds squares.
  - getPiece(move.source) != null (source is occupied by a piece).
  - The move has been validated by the rule pipeline.
Post-condition:
  - getPiece(move.source) == null.
  - getPiece(move.destination) == the piece that previously occupied
    move.source.
  - All other squares are unchanged.
  - game.numMoves has been incremented by one.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Computes the full list of legal moves for the given player on
         the current board. It asks each of the player's pieces for its
         raw candidate moves, then filters every candidate through the
         complete rule pipeline (global rules, protection rule, and
         piece-specific rules) so that only fully valid moves are kept.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty list legal.
  2. For every square (x, y) inside the board:
       a. piece = this.getPiece(x, y).
       b. If piece == null or piece.player != player, skip.
       c. candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, new Place(x, y)).
       d. For each candidate in candidates:
            - Run all global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
              OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule. If any returns false,
              discard the candidate.
            - Run FirstNMovesProtectionRule. If false, discard.
            - Apply piece-specific rules based on the piece type:
                * Knight  -> KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule.
                * Archer  -> ArcherMoveRule.
                * Other   -> no piece-specific rules.
            - If every rule returns true, add candidate to legal.
  3. Return legal.
Related Features: board (read via getPiece), currentPlayer (used to
                  identify which pieces belong to "player"), numMoves
                  (used implicitly by FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
Related Classes: Game, Place, Move, Piece, Knight, Archer, Player,
                 VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule,
                 FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule,
                 ArcherMoveRule, Rule
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are to be enumerated.
                    Must be one of the players registered in the current
                    Configuration.
Output:
  - List<Move> - the moves that the given player may legally execute
                 right now. May be empty if the player is blocked or
                 has no pieces left.
Pre-condition:
  - The board has been initialized from Configuration.
  - All rules referenced are instantiated and stateless.
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and currentPlayer are unchanged.
  - The returned list is a fresh list; the caller may iterate or modify
    it without affecting the game state.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Decides the winner of the game after a move has been executed.
         During the protection phase (game.numMoves <= numMovesProtection)
         no winner may be declared and null is returned. After protection
         ends, a player wins if (1) a Knight leaves the central square,
         or (2) only one player's pieces remain on the board. If the
         current player has no available moves on their turn, the winner
         is the player with the higher score, with ties broken in favor
         of the current player.
Algorithm:
  1. If game.numMoves <= configuration.numMovesProtection, return null
     (protection phase forbids winner evaluation).
  2. Central-square escape check:
       a. If lastMove != null and lastMove.source == centralPlace and
          lastMove.destination != centralPlace and
          lastPiece instanceof Knight,
          return lastPlayer (the player who just moved wins).
  3. Elimination check:
       a. Scan the board and tally distinct piece.player references
          present (using reference identity / equal()).
       b. If only one distinct player owns any piece, return that
          player as the winner.
  4. No-moves check:
       a. If getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer) is empty, compare
          currentPlayer.score with the other player's score.
          - Higher score wins.
          - If scores are equal, currentPlayer wins.
  5. Otherwise return null (game continues).
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer, configuration,
                  configuration.centralPlace, configuration.numMovesProtection,
                  Player.score.
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Place, Move, Piece, Knight, Player
Input:
  - lastPlayer : Player - the player who executed the most recent move.
  - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (used to check Knight
                          type for the central-escape rule).
  - lastMove   : Move   - the move just executed (source/destination
                          are needed for the central-escape test).
Output:
  - Player - the winning player, or null if the game has not yet ended.
Pre-condition:
  - lastMove has already been applied to the board.
  - Scores are up to date.
  - The protection phase is correctly tracked via numMoves and
    numMovesProtection.
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and turn counter are unchanged.
  - Returned value is either null or a non-null Player reference.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and
         destination squares to the moving player's score. The score
         is only updated for a successful (i.e. rule-passing) move;
         a failed attempt leaves both the board and the score
         unchanged.
Algorithm:
  1. Let src = move.source, dst = move.destination.
  2. distance = |src.x - dst.x| + |src.y - dst.y|.
  3. player.score = player.score + distance.
  4. (The piece parameter is not used directly in the arithmetic, but is
     kept in the signature for symmetry with future piece-specific
     scoring and to match the abstract Game contract.)
Related Features: Player.score, configuration (read for board size and
                  central place only as a sanity check; the algorithm
                  itself uses only the Move geometry).
Related Classes: Game, Player, Move, Place
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose score will be increased.
  - piece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (reserved for future
                       piece-specific scoring; currently unused in the
                       arithmetic).
  - move   : Move   - the executed move; only source and destination
                      coordinates are used.
Output:
  - void
Pre-condition:
  - move has been successfully executed (the piece is now at
    move.destination).
  - player is the player who executed the move.
Post-condition:
  - player.score has been increased by
    |move.source.x - move.destination.x| + |move.source.y - move.destination.y|.
  - All other scores are unchanged.
  - The board is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.

JesonMor::start

  3. Loop:
       a. available = this.getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer).
       b. If available is empty:
            - winner = this.getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove)
              using the no-moves / score-tiebreak path.
            - Return winner.
       c. chosen = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, available).
       d. lastPiece  = this.getPiece(chosen.source).
       e. lastMove   = chosen.
       f. this.movePiece(chosen).
       g. this.updateScore(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
       h. this.refreshOutput().
       i. winner = this.getWinner(currentPlayer, lastPiece, lastMove).
          If winner != null, return winner.
       j. Advance currentPlayer to the other player in
          configuration.players (two-player rotation).
  4. (Unreachable in normal play; the loop only exits via return.)
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer, configuration,
                  configuration.players, Player.score.
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Player, Move, Place, Piece,
                 Knight, Archer, ConsolePlayer, RandomPlayer
Input:
  - None (operates entirely on the receiver's configuration field).
Output:
  - Player - the winner of the game once the loop terminates.
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is non-null and has at least two players.
  - The board size is odd, and initial placements are within bounds.
  - configuration.numMovesProtection is non-negative.
  - The Configuration has been validated (else InvalidConfigurationError
    may be thrown during initialization).
Post-condition:
  - The returned Player is one of the players in configuration.players.
  - The board reflects the last executed move.
  - Scores reflect all successfully executed moves.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary: Executes a previously validated move on the board by relocating
         the piece from the move's source square to its destination
         square and clearing the source. The board representation is
         updated in place; this method assumes the move has already
         passed the rule pipeline.
Algorithm:
  1. piece = this.getPiece(move.source).
  2. this.setPiece(move.destination, piece)   // place piece at dst.
  3. this.setPiece(move.source, null)         // vacate the source.
  4. (Optionally) increment game.numMoves to record the executed turn.
     (In the standard loop, the caller / updateScore is responsible for
      this, but the JesonMor implementation increments it here as part
      of movePiece so that FirstNMovesProtectionRule sees the right
      counter on the next validation pass.)
Related Features: board (mutated), numMoves (incremented), currentPlayer
                  (unchanged here, but conceptually the mover).
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - move : Move - the move to execute. Must be a fully legal move
                  (already passed all rules).
Output:
  - void
Pre-condition:
  - move.source and move.destination are both in-bounds squares.
  - getPiece(move.source) != null (source is occupied by a piece).
  - The move has been validated by the rule pipeline.
Post-condition:
  - getPiece(move.source) == null.
  - getPiece(move.destination) == the piece that previously occupied
    move.source.
  - All other squares are unchanged.
  - game.numMoves has been incremented by one.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Computes the full list of legal moves for the given player on
         the current board. It asks each of the player's pieces for its
         raw candidate moves, then filters every candidate through the
         complete rule pipeline (global rules, protection rule, and
         piece-specific rules) so that only fully valid moves are kept.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty list legal.
  2. For every square (x, y) inside the board:
       a. piece = this.getPiece(x, y).
       b. If piece == null or piece.player != player, skip.
       c. candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, new Place(x, y)).
       d. For each candidate in candidates:
            - Run all global rules: VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
              OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule. If any returns false,
              discard the candidate.
            - Run FirstNMovesProtectionRule. If false, discard.
            - Apply piece-specific rules based on the piece type:
                * Knight  -> KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule.
                * Archer  -> ArcherMoveRule.
                * Other   -> no piece-specific rules.
            - If every rule returns true, add candidate to legal.
  3. Return legal.
Related Features: board (read via getPiece), currentPlayer (used to
                  identify which pieces belong to "player"), numMoves
                  (used implicitly by FirstNMovesProtectionRule).
Related Classes: Game, Place, Move, Piece, Knight, Archer, Player,
                 VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule,
                 FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule,
                 ArcherMoveRule, Rule
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are to be enumerated.
                    Must be one of the players registered in the current
                    Configuration.
Output:
  - List<Move> - the moves that the given player may legally execute
                 right now. May be empty if the player is blocked or
                 has no pieces left.
Pre-condition:
  - The board has been initialized from Configuration.
  - All rules referenced are instantiated and stateless.
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and currentPlayer are unchanged.
  - The returned list is a fresh list; the caller may iterate or modify
    it without affecting the game state.

JesonMor::getWinner
Summary: Decides the winner of the game after a move has been executed.
         During the protection phase (game.numMoves <= numMovesProtection)
         no winner may be declared and null is returned. After protection
         ends, a player wins if (1) a Knight leaves the central square,
         or (2) only one player's pieces remain on the board. If the
         current player has no available moves on their turn, the winner
         is the player with the higher score, with ties broken in favor
         of the current player.
Algorithm:
  1. If game.numMoves <= configuration.numMovesProtection, return null
     (protection phase forbids winner evaluation).
  2. Central-square escape check:
       a. If lastMove != null and lastMove.source == centralPlace and
          lastMove.destination != centralPlace and
          lastPiece instanceof Knight,
          return lastPlayer (the player who just moved wins).
  3. Elimination check:
       a. Scan the board and tally distinct piece.player references
          present (using reference identity / equal()).
       b. If only one distinct player owns any piece, return that
          player as the winner.
  4. No-moves check:
       a. If getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer) is empty, compare
          currentPlayer.score with the other player's score.
          - Higher score wins.
          - If scores are equal, currentPlayer wins.
  5. Otherwise return null (game continues).
Related Features: board, numMoves, currentPlayer, configuration,
                  configuration.centralPlace, configuration.numMovesProtection,
                  Player.score.
Related Classes: Game, Configuration, Place, Move, Piece, Knight, Player
Input:
  - lastPlayer : Player - the player who executed the most recent move.
  - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (used to check Knight
                          type for the central-escape rule).
  - lastMove   : Move   - the move just executed (source/destination
                          are needed for the central-escape test).
Output:
  - Player - the winning player, or null if the game has not yet ended.
Pre-condition:
  - lastMove has already been applied to the board.
  - Scores are up to date.
  - The protection phase is correctly tracked via numMoves and
    numMovesProtection.
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and turn counter are unchanged.
  - Returned value is either null or a non-null Player reference.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary: Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and
         destination squares to the moving player's score. The score
         is only updated for a successful (i.e. rule-passing) move;
         a failed attempt leaves both the board and the score
         unchanged.
Algorithm:
  1. Let src = move.source, dst = move.destination.
  2. distance = |src.x - dst.x| + |src.y - dst.y|.
  3. player.score = player.score + distance.
  4. (The piece parameter is not used directly in the arithmetic, but is
     kept in the signature for symmetry with future piece-specific
     scoring and to match the abstract Game contract.)
Related Features: Player.score, configuration (read for board size and
                  central place only as a sanity check; the algorithm
                  itself uses only the Move geometry).
Related Classes: Game, Player, Move, Place
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose score will be increased.
  - piece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (reserved for future
                       piece-specific scoring; currently unused in the
                       arithmetic).
  - move   : Move   - the executed move; only source and destination
                      coordinates are used.
Output:
  - void
Pre-condition:
  - move has been successfully executed (the piece is now at
    move.destination).
  - player is the player who executed the move.
Post-condition:
  - player.score has been increased by
    |move.source.x - move.destination.x| + |move.source.y - move.destination.y|.
  - All other scores are unchanged.
  - The board is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in <Operations> with a specfication.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```
