# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::getWinner
Summary:
  Decides the winner of the game after a successful move (or after a
  no-moves end-of-game state) according to the rules: no winner may
  be declared during the protection phase, a Knight leaving the
  central place wins, eliminating all opponent pieces wins, and when
  no moves are available the higher score wins (ties go to the
  current player).
Algorithm:
  numProt = configuration.numMovesProtection
  if game.numMoves < numProt:
      return null                       // protection phase forbids any winner
  // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
  central = configuration.centralPlace
  if lastPiece is Knight and
     lastMove.source == central and
     lastMove.destination != central:
      return lastPlayer
  // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
  counts = map from Player to count of pieces still on the board
  remaining = number of players in counts with count > 0
  if remaining == 1:
      return the unique player in counts with count > 0
  // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to
  // lastPlayer (i.e., the player who last acted / current player when
  // moves are exhausted).
  p0 = configuration.players[0]
  p1 = configuration.players[1]
  if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
  if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
  return lastPlayer                    // tie -> current/last player wins
Related Features:
  - board         : PieceArray2D - used to count pieces by player.
  - configuration : Configuration - provides numMovesProtection,
                             centralPlace, and the list of players
                             (and their scores).
  - numMoves      : int - compared with numMovesProtection to gate
                         the protection phase.
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Move, Place, Piece, Configuration, Knight
Input:
  - lastPlayer : Player - the player who just executed (or attempted)
                           the last move; used for the "Knight leaves
                           central" check and as the tie-breaker.
  - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved last; must be a
                           Knight to satisfy the central-exit win.
  - lastMove   : Move   - the move that was just executed; its
                           source/destination drive the central-exit
                           check.
Output:
  - Player  - the winning player, or null if no winner can yet be
              declared (still inside the protection phase, or none
              of the win conditions are met).
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is initialized; configuration.centralPlace and
    configuration.players are populated.
  - game.numMoves is up to date (incremented after each successful
    move).
  - lastPlayer, lastPiece, and lastMove describe the most recent
    successful move (or appropriate sentinels for the no-moves
    case handled by the caller).
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and numMoves are not modified.
  - Returns null when the game continues, or a non-null Player
    indicating the winner.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary:
  Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination
  to the given player's score. Called only after a move has been
  successfully executed (i.e., it passed all applicable rules).
Algorithm:
  dx = abs(move.destination.x - move.source.x)
  dy = abs(move.destination.y - move.source.y)
  player.score = player.score + dx + dy
Related Features:
  - (no Game/JesonMor internal feature is read or written; the only
    mutable state lives on the supplied Player.)
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Move, Place
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose score will be increased;
                     must be the player who just executed the move.
  - piece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (kept on the signature
                      for symmetry with the class diagram; not used
                      in the score calculation itself).
  - move   : Move   - the move that was executed; its source and
                      destination determine the Manhattan distance.
Output:
  - void - the effect is a mutation of player.score.
Pre-condition:
  - player and move are non-null.
  - The move has already been validated and applied to the board.
  - move.source and move.destination are in-bounds Places.
Post-condition:
  - player.score has been incremented by the Manhattan distance
    |dst.x - src.x| + |dst.y - src.y|.
  - The board, numMoves, and the opponent's score are unchanged.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary:
  Physically executes a move on the board: takes the piece at the
  source square, places it at the destination square, and clears the
  source square. This method is invoked only after a move has passed
  the full rule pipeline, so the source is guaranteed to contain a
  piece and the destination is either empty or holds an opponent's
  piece (which is overwritten).
Algorithm:
  piece = game.getPiece(move.source)    // read via the API
  game.setPiece(move.destination, piece) // write via the API
  game.setPiece(move.source, null)      // clear the source
Related Features:
  - board : PieceArray2D - the 2D board mutated by this operation.
                          All reads and writes go through
                          Game.getPiece / Game.setPiece, never
                          via direct board indexing.
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - move : Move - the move to execute. move.source is the square
                  holding the piece to move; move.destination is
                  the target square. Both must be in-bounds Places.
Output:
  - void - no return value; the effect is observed on the board.
Pre-condition:
  - The move has been validated by the full rule pipeline.
  - move.source is within the board and currently holds a piece.
  - move.destination is within the board and either empty or
    occupied by an opponent's piece.
Post-condition:
  - move.destination now holds the piece that was at move.source.
  - move.source is empty (null).
  - The board reflects the post-move state; scores, numMoves, and
    the current player are unchanged by this method.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary:
  Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
  generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
  board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
  rule (global, protection, and piece-specific). The returned list is
  used by ConsolePlayer/RandomPlayer and by the win-condition check
  that detects "no available moves" situations.
Algorithm:
  result = empty list
  size = configuration.size
  for x in [0, size):
      for y in [0, size):
          piece = getPiece(x, y)
          if piece == null or piece.player != player:
              continue
          src = new Place(x, y)
          candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(game, src)
          for each move m in candidates:
              if not (VacantRule.validate(game, m) and
                      NilMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
                      OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, m) and
                      OccupiedRule.validate(game, m) and
                      FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, m)):
                  continue
              // piece-specific rules
              if piece is Knight:
                  if not (KnightMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
                          KnightBlockRule.validate(game, m)):
                      continue
              elif piece is Archer:
                  if not ArcherMoveRule.validate(game, m):
                      continue
              // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
              result.add(m)
  return result
Related Features:
  - board         : PieceArray2D - the 2D board queried for the player's pieces.
  - configuration : Configuration - provides the board size.
  - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is (used for
                             context; the method is parameterized by
                             `player`).
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration, Rule, VacantRule,
  NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule,
  KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are being enumerated.
                     Must be one of configuration.players.
Output:
  - List<Move> - the set of all legal moves currently available to
                 `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
                 holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
                 that satisfies every applicable validation rule.
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is set and configuration.size is a positive odd
    integer; configuration.players contains `player`.
  - The board has been initialized consistent with configuration.
Post-condition:
  - The returned list contains exactly the moves that would pass the
    full rule pipeline for the current board and game state.
  - No mutation of the board, scores, or numMoves occurs.

JesonMor::start
Summary:
  Drives the complete turn-based game loop. Initializes state, alternates
  turns, fetches legal moves, asks the current Player for a choice via
  Player.nextMove, executes the move, updates the score, refreshes the
  console, and evaluates the win condition. Returns the Player who
  wins the game (or the score-comparison winner if a player has no
  available moves).
Algorithm:
  // initial setup (configuration provides board, players, numMovesProtection)
  currentPlayer = configuration.players[0]
  numMoves = 0
  refreshOutput()
  while true:
      availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer)
      if availableMoves is empty:
          // no-moves end-of-game: higher score wins, ties to currentPlayer
          p0 = configuration.players[0]; p1 = configuration.players[1]
          if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
          if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
          return currentPlayer
      chosen = currentPlayer.nextMove(game, availableMoves)
      piece = getPiece(chosen.source)
      movePiece(chosen)
      updateScore(currentPlayer, piece, chosen)
      numMoves = numMoves + 1
      refreshOutput()
      winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, piece, chosen)
      if winner != null:
          return winner
      // switch to the other player
      if currentPlayer == configuration.players[0]:
          currentPlayer = configuration.players[1]
      else:
          currentPlayer = configuration.players[0]
Related Features:
  - configuration : Configuration - provides the initial board,
                             players, central place, and
                             numMovesProtection.
  - board         : PieceArray2D - inspected/updated through
                             getPiece/movePiece.
  - numMoves      : int - tracks how many successful moves have
                         been made; gates the protection phase.
  - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is; toggled
                             each iteration.
Related Classes:
  Game, Configuration, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Knight, Archer,
  Rule
Input:
  - (none beyond the inherited state) - all input is read through
    configuration (board, players, numMovesProtection) and through
    the current Player's nextMove call (which for ConsolePlayer
    reads a zero-based index from System.in).
Output:
  - Player - the player who has won the game. The method terminates
             only when a winner can be declared (via the post-move
             rule check or the no-moves score tie-break).
Pre-condition:
  - configuration has been set with a valid odd board size, an
    initial board, a non-empty list of players (typically two), and
    a non-negative numMovesProtection.
  - No piece access via direct board indexing; the board is reached
    exclusively through Game.getPiece / Game.setPiece.
Post-condition:
  - The board reflects the final move of the game.
  - Player scores reflect all scored moves performed during the
    game (each successful move adds its Manhattan distance).
  - The returned Player is the winner per the documented rules.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
JesonMor::getWinner
Summary:
  Decides the winner of the game after a successful move (or after a
  no-moves end-of-game state) according to the rules: no winner may
  be declared during the protection phase, a Knight leaving the
  central place wins, eliminating all opponent pieces wins, and when
  no moves are available the higher score wins (ties go to the
  current player).
Algorithm:
  numProt = configuration.numMovesProtection
  if game.numMoves < numProt:
      return null                       // protection phase forbids any winner
  // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
  central = configuration.centralPlace
  if lastPiece is Knight and
     lastMove.source == central and
     lastMove.destination != central:
      return lastPlayer
  // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
  counts = map from Player to count of pieces still on the board
  remaining = number of players in counts with count > 0
  if remaining == 1:
      return the unique player in counts with count > 0
  // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to
  // lastPlayer (i.e., the player who last acted / current player when
  // moves are exhausted).
  p0 = configuration.players[0]
  p1 = configuration.players[1]
  if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
  if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
  return lastPlayer                    // tie -> current/last player wins
Related Features:
  - board         : PieceArray2D - used to count pieces by player.
  - configuration : Configuration - provides numMovesProtection,
                             centralPlace, and the list of players
                             (and their scores).
  - numMoves      : int - compared with numMovesProtection to gate
                         the protection phase.
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Move, Place, Piece, Configuration, Knight
Input:
  - lastPlayer : Player - the player who just executed (or attempted)
                           the last move; used for the "Knight leaves
                           central" check and as the tie-breaker.
  - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved last; must be a
                           Knight to satisfy the central-exit win.
  - lastMove   : Move   - the move that was just executed; its
                           source/destination drive the central-exit
                           check.
Output:
  - Player  - the winning player, or null if no winner can yet be
              declared (still inside the protection phase, or none
              of the win conditions are met).
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is initialized; configuration.centralPlace and
    configuration.players are populated.
  - game.numMoves is up to date (incremented after each successful
    move).
  - lastPlayer, lastPiece, and lastMove describe the most recent
    successful move (or appropriate sentinels for the no-moves
    case handled by the caller).
Post-condition:
  - The board, scores, and numMoves are not modified.
  - Returns null when the game continues, or a non-null Player
    indicating the winner.

JesonMor::updateScore
Summary:
  Adds the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination
  to the given player's score. Called only after a move has been
  successfully executed (i.e., it passed all applicable rules).
Algorithm:
  dx = abs(move.destination.x - move.source.x)
  dy = abs(move.destination.y - move.source.y)
  player.score = player.score + dx + dy
Related Features:
  - (no Game/JesonMor internal feature is read or written; the only
    mutable state lives on the supplied Player.)
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Move, Place
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose score will be increased;
                     must be the player who just executed the move.
  - piece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved (kept on the signature
                      for symmetry with the class diagram; not used
                      in the score calculation itself).
  - move   : Move   - the move that was executed; its source and
                      destination determine the Manhattan distance.
Output:
  - void - the effect is a mutation of player.score.
Pre-condition:
  - player and move are non-null.
  - The move has already been validated and applied to the board.
  - move.source and move.destination are in-bounds Places.
Post-condition:
  - player.score has been incremented by the Manhattan distance
    |dst.x - src.x| + |dst.y - src.y|.
  - The board, numMoves, and the opponent's score are unchanged.

JesonMor::movePiece
Summary:
  Physically executes a move on the board: takes the piece at the
  source square, places it at the destination square, and clears the
  source square. This method is invoked only after a move has passed
  the full rule pipeline, so the source is guaranteed to contain a
  piece and the destination is either empty or holds an opponent's
  piece (which is overwritten).
Algorithm:
  piece = game.getPiece(move.source)    // read via the API
  game.setPiece(move.destination, piece) // write via the API
  game.setPiece(move.source, null)      // clear the source
Related Features:
  - board : PieceArray2D - the 2D board mutated by this operation.
                          All reads and writes go through
                          Game.getPiece / Game.setPiece, never
                          via direct board indexing.
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - move : Move - the move to execute. move.source is the square
                  holding the piece to move; move.destination is
                  the target square. Both must be in-bounds Places.
Output:
  - void - no return value; the effect is observed on the board.
Pre-condition:
  - The move has been validated by the full rule pipeline.
  - move.source is within the board and currently holds a piece.
  - move.destination is within the board and either empty or
    occupied by an opponent's piece.
Post-condition:
  - move.destination now holds the piece that was at move.source.
  - move.source is empty (null).
  - The board reflects the post-move state; scores, numMoves, and
    the current player are unchanged by this method.

JesonMor::getAvailableMoves
Summary:
  Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
  generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
  board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
  rule (global, protection, and piece-specific). The returned list is
  used by ConsolePlayer/RandomPlayer and by the win-condition check
  that detects "no available moves" situations.
Algorithm:
  result = empty list
  size = configuration.size
  for x in [0, size):
      for y in [0, size):
          piece = getPiece(x, y)
          if piece == null or piece.player != player:
              continue
          src = new Place(x, y)
          candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(game, src)
          for each move m in candidates:
              if not (VacantRule.validate(game, m) and
                      NilMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
                      OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, m) and
                      OccupiedRule.validate(game, m) and
                      FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, m)):
                  continue
              // piece-specific rules
              if piece is Knight:
                  if not (KnightMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
                          KnightBlockRule.validate(game, m)):
                      continue
              elif piece is Archer:
                  if not ArcherMoveRule.validate(game, m):
                      continue
              // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
              result.add(m)
  return result
Related Features:
  - board         : PieceArray2D - the 2D board queried for the player's pieces.
  - configuration : Configuration - provides the board size.
  - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is (used for
                             context; the method is parameterized by
                             `player`).
Related Classes:
  Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration, Rule, VacantRule,
  NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule,
  KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
Input:
  - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are being enumerated.
                     Must be one of configuration.players.
Output:
  - List<Move> - the set of all legal moves currently available to
                 `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
                 holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
                 that satisfies every applicable validation rule.
Pre-condition:
  - configuration is set and configuration.size is a positive odd
    integer; configuration.players contains `player`.
  - The board has been initialized consistent with configuration.
Post-condition:
  - The returned list contains exactly the moves that would pass the
    full rule pipeline for the current board and game state.
  - No mutation of the board, scores, or numMoves occurs.

JesonMor::start
Summary:
  Drives the complete turn-based game loop. Initializes state, alternates
  turns, fetches legal moves, asks the current Player for a choice via
  Player.nextMove, executes the move, updates the score, refreshes the
  console, and evaluates the win condition. Returns the Player who
  wins the game (or the score-comparison winner if a player has no
  available moves).
Algorithm:
  // initial setup (configuration provides board, players, numMovesProtection)
  currentPlayer = configuration.players[0]
  numMoves = 0
  refreshOutput()
  while true:
      availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer)
      if availableMoves is empty:
          // no-moves end-of-game: higher score wins, ties to currentPlayer
          p0 = configuration.players[0]; p1 = configuration.players[1]
          if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
          if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
          return currentPlayer
      chosen = currentPlayer.nextMove(game, availableMoves)
      piece = getPiece(chosen.source)
      movePiece(chosen)
      updateScore(currentPlayer, piece, chosen)
      numMoves = numMoves + 1
      refreshOutput()
      winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, piece, chosen)
      if winner != null:
          return winner
      // switch to the other player
      if currentPlayer == configuration.players[0]:
          currentPlayer = configuration.players[1]
      else:
          currentPlayer = configuration.players[0]
Related Features:
  - configuration : Configuration - provides the initial board,
                             players, central place, and
                             numMovesProtection.
  - board         : PieceArray2D - inspected/updated through
                             getPiece/movePiece.
  - numMoves      : int - tracks how many successful moves have
                         been made; gates the protection phase.
  - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is; toggled
                             each iteration.
Related Classes:
  Game, Configuration, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Knight, Archer,
  Rule
Input:
  - (none beyond the inherited state) - all input is read through
    configuration (board, players, numMovesProtection) and through
    the current Player's nextMove call (which for ConsolePlayer
    reads a zero-based index from System.in).
Output:
  - Player - the player who has won the game. The method terminates
             only when a winner can be declared (via the post-move
             rule check or the no-moves score tie-break).
Pre-condition:
  - configuration has been set with a valid odd board size, an
    initial board, a non-empty list of players (typically two), and
    a non-negative numMovesProtection.
  - No piece access via direct board indexing; the board is reached
    exclusively through Game.getPiece / Game.setPiece.
Post-condition:
  - The board reflects the final move of the game.
  - Player scores reflect all scored moves performed during the
    game (each successful move adds its Manhattan distance).
  - The returned Player is the winner per the documented rules.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
OccupiedRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose destination already contains
  a piece belonging to the same player as the source piece
  ("friendly fire"). Empty destinations and destinations occupied by
  an opponent's piece are both allowed by this rule (the protection
  rule and piece-specific rules then decide whether a capture is
  actually legal).
Algorithm:
  srcPiece = game.getPiece(move.source)
  if srcPiece == null:
      return false                      // VacantRule should reject this
  dstPiece = game.getPiece(move.destination)
  if dstPiece == null:
      return true                       // empty destination is fine
  return dstPiece.player != srcPiece.player   // opponent's piece is allowed
Related Features:
  None (OccupiedRule has no attributes; it inspects only the board
  through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece, Player
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to read the source
                  and destination pieces.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if the destination is empty or occupied by an
               opponent's piece; false if the destination is occupied
               by a piece of the same player as the source piece
               (or if the source is unexpectedly empty).
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized; getPiece is callable for any in-bounds
    coordinate.
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Operation Specifications
OccupiedRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose destination already contains
  a piece belonging to the same player as the source piece
  ("friendly fire"). Empty destinations and destinations occupied by
  an opponent's piece are both allowed by this rule (the protection
  rule and piece-specific rules then decide whether a capture is
  actually legal).
Algorithm:
  srcPiece = game.getPiece(move.source)
  if srcPiece == null:
      return false                      // VacantRule should reject this
  dstPiece = game.getPiece(move.destination)
  if dstPiece == null:
      return true                       // empty destination is fine
  return dstPiece.player != srcPiece.player   // opponent's piece is allowed
Related Features:
  None (OccupiedRule has no attributes; it inspects only the board
  through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece, Player
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to read the source
                  and destination pieces.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if the destination is empty or occupied by an
               opponent's piece; false if the destination is occupied
               by a piece of the same player as the source piece
               (or if the source is unexpectedly empty).
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized; getPiece is callable for any in-bounds
    coordinate.
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
OutOfBoundaryRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose source or destination lies
  outside the square board. The board size is read from the active
  Configuration.
Algorithm:
  size = game.configuration.size
  for p in {move.source, move.destination}:
      if p == null:
          return false
      if p.x < 0 or p.x >= size or p.y < 0 or p.y >= size:
          return false
  return true
Related Features:
  None (OutOfBoundaryRule has no attributes; it relies on
  configuration read through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Configuration
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, providing
                  game.configuration.size.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    are checked against the board bounds.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if both source and destination are in-bounds;
               false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized and configuration.size is a positive
    integer.
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Operation Specifications
OutOfBoundaryRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose source or destination lies
  outside the square board. The board size is read from the active
  Configuration.
Algorithm:
  size = game.configuration.size
  for p in {move.source, move.destination}:
      if p == null:
          return false
      if p.x < 0 or p.x >= size or p.y < 0 or p.y >= size:
          return false
  return true
Related Features:
  None (OutOfBoundaryRule has no attributes; it relies on
  configuration read through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Configuration
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, providing
                  game.configuration.size.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    are checked against the board bounds.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if both source and destination are in-bounds;
               false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized and configuration.size is a positive
    integer.
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
RandomPlayer::nextMove
Summary:
  Selects and returns a uniformly random Move from the supplied
  pre-computed list of legal moves for the current player. The list
  is guaranteed to be non-empty by the caller (JesonMor::start), so
  no empty-list handling is required.
Algorithm:
  index = a uniformly random integer in [0, availableMoves.size())
  return availableMoves.get(index)
Related Features:
  None (RandomPlayer does not read its own color/name/score; the
  decision depends only on the availableMoves list).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game instance (part of the Player
                   contract; not consulted in this implementation).
  - availableMoves : List<Move> - non-empty list of legal moves for
                                   the current player.
Output:
  - Move - one of the entries in availableMoves, chosen at random.
Pre-condition:
  - availableMoves is non-null and non-empty (the caller only
    invokes nextMove when at least one legal move exists).
Post-condition:
  - The selected Move is returned; the list itself is not mutated.
  - Player score, board, and numMoves are unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
RandomPlayer::nextMove
Summary:
  Selects and returns a uniformly random Move from the supplied
  pre-computed list of legal moves for the current player. The list
  is guaranteed to be non-empty by the caller (JesonMor::start), so
  no empty-list handling is required.
Algorithm:
  index = a uniformly random integer in [0, availableMoves.size())
  return availableMoves.get(index)
Related Features:
  None (RandomPlayer does not read its own color/name/score; the
  decision depends only on the availableMoves list).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game instance (part of the Player
                   contract; not consulted in this implementation).
  - availableMoves : List<Move> - non-empty list of legal moves for
                                   the current player.
Output:
  - Move - one of the entries in availableMoves, chosen at random.
Pre-condition:
  - availableMoves is non-null and non-empty (the caller only
    invokes nextMove when at least one legal move exists).
Post-condition:
  - The selected Move is returned; the list itself is not mutated.
  - Player score, board, and numMoves are unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
ArcherMoveRule::validate
Summary:
  Validates that a candidate move is a legal Archer move: the move must
  travel along a single orthogonal axis, and either the path between
  source and destination must be completely clear (non-capturing) or
  there must be exactly one piece of any color acting as a "screen"
  between source and destination (capturing, Cannon-style).
Algorithm:
  src = move.source
  dst = move.destination
  if src == null or dst == null:
      return false
  // must be on the same row or the same column, but not both
  if (src.x == dst.x) == (src.y == dst.y):
      return false
  // count pieces strictly between src and dst on the orthogonal line
  between = 0
  if src.x == dst.x:                    // vertical move
      lo = min(src.y, dst.y) + 1
      hi = max(src.y, dst.y) - 1
      for y in [lo, hi]:
          if game.getPiece(src.x, y) != null:
              between = between + 1
  else:                                 // horizontal move
      lo = min(src.x, dst.x) + 1
      hi = max(src.x, dst.x) - 1
      for x in [lo, hi]:
          if game.getPiece(x, src.y) != null:
              between = between + 1
  dstPiece = game.getPiece(dst)
  if dstPiece == null:
      return between == 0                // non-capturing requires clear path
  else:
      return between == 1                // capturing requires exactly one screen
Related Features:
  None (ArcherMoveRule carries no attributes; the rule only inspects the
  board through the supplied Game reference).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to inspect the squares
                  between and at the destination via getPiece(...).
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    define the orthogonal path to be checked.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if and only if the move is a legal Archer move
               (orthogonal, with either a clear path for non-captures
               or exactly one screen piece for captures); false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
  - game is initialized so that getPiece can be called for any in-bounds
    coordinate (0 <= x,y < size).
Post-condition:
  - Returns true only when the move geometry matches the Archer
    sliding/capture model. The rule does not mutate the board or the
    move object.

# Operation Specifications
ArcherMoveRule::validate
Summary:
  Validates that a candidate move is a legal Archer move: the move must
  travel along a single orthogonal axis, and either the path between
  source and destination must be completely clear (non-capturing) or
  there must be exactly one piece of any color acting as a "screen"
  between source and destination (capturing, Cannon-style).
Algorithm:
  src = move.source
  dst = move.destination
  if src == null or dst == null:
      return false
  // must be on the same row or the same column, but not both
  if (src.x == dst.x) == (src.y == dst.y):
      return false
  // count pieces strictly between src and dst on the orthogonal line
  between = 0
  if src.x == dst.x:                    // vertical move
      lo = min(src.y, dst.y) + 1
      hi = max(src.y, dst.y) - 1
      for y in [lo, hi]:
          if game.getPiece(src.x, y) != null:
              between = between + 1
  else:                                 // horizontal move
      lo = min(src.x, dst.x) + 1
      hi = max(src.x, dst.x) - 1
      for x in [lo, hi]:
          if game.getPiece(x, src.y) != null:
              between = between + 1
  dstPiece = game.getPiece(dst)
  if dstPiece == null:
      return between == 0                // non-capturing requires clear path
  else:
      return between == 1                // capturing requires exactly one screen
Related Features:
  None (ArcherMoveRule carries no attributes; the rule only inspects the
  board through the supplied Game reference).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to inspect the squares
                  between and at the destination via getPiece(...).
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    define the orthogonal path to be checked.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if and only if the move is a legal Archer move
               (orthogonal, with either a clear path for non-captures
               or exactly one screen piece for captures); false otherwise.
Pre-condition:
  - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
  - game is initialized so that getPiece can be called for any in-bounds
    coordinate (0 <= x,y < size).
Post-condition:
  - Returns true only when the move geometry matches the Archer
    sliding/capture model. The rule does not mutate the board or the
    move object.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
NilMoveRule::validate
Summary:
  Rejects "null" or no-op moves where source and destination are
  the same square. This is a global rule applied to every candidate
  move regardless of piece type.
Algorithm:
  return move.source != move.destination
Related Features:
  None (NilMoveRule carries no attributes; it inspects the Move
  object only).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state (not consulted by this
                  rule, kept for the Rule interface).
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    are compared.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if the move actually changes square; false if
               source and destination are equal.
Pre-condition:
  - move is non-null and move.source / move.destination are
    non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Operation Specifications
NilMoveRule::validate
Summary:
  Rejects "null" or no-op moves where source and destination are
  the same square. This is a global rule applied to every candidate
  move regardless of piece type.
Algorithm:
  return move.source != move.destination
Related Features:
  None (NilMoveRule carries no attributes; it inspects the Move
  object only).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state (not consulted by this
                  rule, kept for the Rule interface).
  - move  : Move - the candidate move whose source and destination
                    are compared.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if the move actually changes square; false if
               source and destination are equal.
Pre-condition:
  - move is non-null and move.source / move.destination are
    non-null Places.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.
