# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
VacantRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose source square is empty. A
  legal move must always originate from a square containing a piece.
Algorithm:
  return game.getPiece(move.source) != null
Related Features:
  None (VacantRule carries no attributes; the rule inspects only
  the board through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to read the piece
                  at move.source.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move; only its source is
                    consulted.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if move.source is occupied by any piece; false
               if it is empty.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized; getPiece is callable for any in-bounds
    coordinate.
  - move.source is a non-null Place.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Operation Specifications
VacantRule::validate
Summary:
  Global rule that rejects moves whose source square is empty. A
  legal move must always originate from a square containing a piece.
Algorithm:
  return game.getPiece(move.source) != null
Related Features:
  None (VacantRule carries no attributes; the rule inspects only
  the board through the supplied Game).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Piece
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used to read the piece
                  at move.source.
  - move  : Move - the candidate move; only its source is
                    consulted.
Output:
  - boolean  - true if move.source is occupied by any piece; false
               if it is empty.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized; getPiece is callable for any in-bounds
    coordinate.
  - move.source is a non-null Place.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the rule is a pure predicate.

# Requirement
```text
 Overview

  This project implements a customized board game called JesonMor. It is a turn-based, two-player game played on a
  square grid board of odd size (e.g., 9x9). The game features two types of pieces: Knight and Archer, each with unique
  movement and capture mechanics inspired by Western and Chinese chess. Players take turns moving their pieces,
  accumulating a score based on the Manhattan distance of each move. The game incorporates a rule-based validation
  pipeline to ensure all moves are legal. The game also includes a protection phase for the first N moves where
  capturing is prohibited. The system provides the core game loop, piece movement logic, and rule validations.

  Functional Requirements

  Game Control and Loop (JesonMor)

  Game Initialization: The game starts by loading a Configuration which provides the board size (must be odd), initial
  piece placements, players, central place (located at size/2, size/2), and the number of protected moves.

  Turn-Based Execution: Implement a continuous game loop where players take turns sequentially. In each turn, fetch the
  available moves for the current player, prompt the player to make a choice (via Player.nextMove), execute the move,
  update the player's score, and refresh the console output.

  Move Execution: When a move is executed, the piece at the source square must be moved to the destination square on the
   2D board array. The source square becomes empty (null).

  Score Calculation: After a successful move, the current player's score increases by the Manhattan distance between the
   source and destination squares. A move is executed and scored only if it passes all applicable rules; otherwise the board state and scores remain
  unchanged for that attempt.

  Win Condition: After each move, evaluate if a player has won. No winner can be declared within the first
  numMovesProtection moves. After protection, a player wins
   if either:
  1. A Knight leaves the central square (source is central place and destination is not central place), or
  2. Only one player's pieces remain on the board (all opponent pieces have been captured).
  Additionally, if a player has no available moves on their turn, the game ends and the winner is decided by score
  comparison: the player with higher score wins; if scores are equal, the current player wins.

  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
Piece::getAvailableMoves
Summary:
  Abstract contract for generating the set of structurally-valid
  candidate moves for a Piece at a given source square. Subclasses
  (Knight, Archer) implement the piece-specific geometry. The
  returned list contains raw candidates and is not filtered by any
  global or piece-specific rule; rule filtering is performed by the
  caller (e.g., JesonMor::getAvailableMoves).
Algorithm:
  // abstract; subclass-defined
  return List<Move> of candidate moves
Related Features:
  None (the abstract base class has no geometry; subclasses provide
  the implementation).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Configuration (and the concrete subclasses
  Knight, Archer)
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used by subclasses to
                   query board size and (potentially) the board.
  - source : Place - the current position of the piece (0-based,
                       x = column, y = row, bottom-left origin).
Output:
  - List<Move> - candidate moves whose source equals the input
                 source. The size and shape of the list depend on
                 the concrete piece type. May be empty.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized so that subclasses can read board size and
    inspect the board.
  - source is a non-null Place within the board.
Post-condition:
  - The returned Move objects all share source == source.
  - No global or piece-specific rule filtering has been applied.
  - No game state is mutated.

Piece::getLabel
Summary:
  Abstract contract that returns the single-character label used to
  render a Piece on the console board. Concrete piece types map to
  fixed characters: Knight -> 'K', Archer -> 'A'. The method does
  not take the piece's color into account; coloring is applied at
  display time.
Algorithm:
  // abstract; subclass-defined
  return a char label
Related Features:
  None (Piece has no class-level attributes; the label is determined
  entirely by the concrete subclass).
Related Classes:
  None (the method depends only on the concrete subclass; it does
  not call into Game, Player, or any other class in the diagram).
Input:
  - (none) - the method is parameterless.
Output:
  - char - the piece's display label, e.g., 'K' for Knight,
           'A' for Archer.
Pre-condition:
  - The receiver is a non-null Piece instance.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the method is a pure function of the
    receiver's runtime type.

# Operation Specifications
Piece::getAvailableMoves
Summary:
  Abstract contract for generating the set of structurally-valid
  candidate moves for a Piece at a given source square. Subclasses
  (Knight, Archer) implement the piece-specific geometry. The
  returned list contains raw candidates and is not filtered by any
  global or piece-specific rule; rule filtering is performed by the
  caller (e.g., JesonMor::getAvailableMoves).
Algorithm:
  // abstract; subclass-defined
  return List<Move> of candidate moves
Related Features:
  None (the abstract base class has no geometry; subclasses provide
  the implementation).
Related Classes:
  Game, Move, Place, Configuration (and the concrete subclasses
  Knight, Archer)
Input:
  - game : Game - the current game state, used by subclasses to
                   query board size and (potentially) the board.
  - source : Place - the current position of the piece (0-based,
                       x = column, y = row, bottom-left origin).
Output:
  - List<Move> - candidate moves whose source equals the input
                 source. The size and shape of the list depend on
                 the concrete piece type. May be empty.
Pre-condition:
  - game is initialized so that subclasses can read board size and
    inspect the board.
  - source is a non-null Place within the board.
Post-condition:
  - The returned Move objects all share source == source.
  - No global or piece-specific rule filtering has been applied.
  - No game state is mutated.

Piece::getLabel
Summary:
  Abstract contract that returns the single-character label used to
  render a Piece on the console board. Concrete piece types map to
  fixed characters: Knight -> 'K', Archer -> 'A'. The method does
  not take the piece's color into account; coloring is applied at
  display time.
Algorithm:
  // abstract; subclass-defined
  return a char label
Related Features:
  None (Piece has no class-level attributes; the label is determined
  entirely by the concrete subclass).
Related Classes:
  None (the method depends only on the concrete subclass; it does
  not call into Game, Player, or any other class in the diagram).
Input:
  - (none) - the method is parameterless.
Output:
  - char - the piece's display label, e.g., 'K' for Knight,
           'A' for Archer.
Pre-condition:
  - The receiver is a non-null Piece instance.
Post-condition:
  - No state is modified; the method is a pure function of the
    receiver's runtime type.

```java
   *   Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
   *   generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
   *   board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
```

```java
  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Decides the winner of the game after a successful move (or after a
   *   no-moves end-of-game state) according to the rules: no winner may
   *   be declared during the protection phase, a Knight leaving the
   *   central place wins, eliminating all opponent pieces wins, and when
   *   no moves are available the higher score wins (ties go to the
   *   current player).
   * Algorithm:
   *   numProt = configuration.numMovesProtection
   *   if game.numMoves < numProt:
   *       return null                       // protection phase forbids any winner
   *   // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
   *   central = configuration.centralPlace
   *   if lastPiece is Knight and
   *      lastMove.source == central and
   *      lastMove.destination != central:
   *       return lastPlayer
   *   // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
   *   counts = map from Player to count of pieces still on the board
   *   remaining = number of players in counts with count > 0
   *   if remaining == 1:
   *       return the unique player in counts with count > 0
   *   // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to
   *   // lastPlayer (i.e., the player who last acted / current player when
   *   // moves are exhausted).
   *   p0 = configuration.players[0]
   *   p1 = configuration.players[1]
   *   if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
   *   if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
   *   return lastPlayer                    // tie -> current/last player wins
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - used to count pieces by player.
   *   - configuration : Configuration - provides numMovesProtection,
   *                              centralPlace, and the list of players
   *                              (and their scores).
   *   - numMoves      : int - compared with numMovesProtection to gate
   *                          the protection phase.
   * Related Classes:
   *   Game, Player, Move, Place, Piece, Configuration, Knight
   * Input:
   *   - lastPlayer : Player - the player who just executed (or attempted)
   *                            the last move; used for the "Knight leaves
   *                            central" check and as the tie-breaker.
   *   - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved last; must be a
   *                            Knight to satisfy the central-exit win.
   *   - lastMove   : Move   - the move that was just executed; its
   *                            source/destination drive the central-exit
   *                            check.
   * Output:
   *   - Player  - the winning player, or null if no winner can yet be
   *               declared (still inside the protection phase, or none
   *               of the win conditions are met).
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - configuration is initialized; configuration.centralPlace and
   *     configuration.players are populated.
   *   - game.numMoves is up to date (incremented after each successful
   *     move).
   *   - lastPlayer, lastPiece, and lastMove describe the most recent
   *     successful move (or appropriate sentinels for the no-moves

   * Post-condition:

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
   *   generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
   *   board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
   *   rule (global, protection, and piece-specific). The returned list is
   *   used by ConsolePlayer/RandomPlayer and by the win-condition check
   *   that detects "no available moves" situations.
   * Algorithm:
   *   result = empty list
   *   size = configuration.size
   *   for x in [0, size):
   *       for y in [0, size):
   *           piece = getPiece(x, y)
   *           if piece == null or piece.player != player:
   *               continue
   *           src = new Place(x, y)
   *           candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(game, src)
   *           for each move m in candidates:
   *               if not (VacantRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       NilMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OccupiedRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                   continue
   *               // piece-specific rules
   *               if piece is Knight:
   *                   if not (KnightMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                           KnightBlockRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                       continue
   *               elif piece is Archer:
   *                   if not ArcherMoveRule.validate(game, m):
   *                       continue
   *               // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
   *               result.add(m)
   *   return result
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - the 2D board queried for the player's pieces.
   *   - configuration : Configuration - provides the board size.
   *   - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is (used for
   *                              context; the method is parameterized by
   *                              `player`).
   * Related Classes:

   *   NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule,
   *   KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
   * Input:
   *   - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are being enumerated.
   *                      Must be one of configuration.players.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - the set of all legal moves currently available to
   *                  `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
   *                  holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
   *                  that satisfies every applicable validation rule.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - configuration is set and configuration.size is a positive odd
   *     integer; configuration.players contains `player`.
```

```java
   *       if availableMoves is empty:
   *           // no-moves end-of-game: higher score wins, ties to currentPlayer
   *           p0 = configuration.players[0]; p1 = configuration.players[1]

   *           if p1.score > p0.score: return p1

   *       movePiece(chosen)

   *       numMoves = numMoves + 1
   *       refreshOutput()

   *       if winner != null:
   *           return winner
   *       // switch to the other player
   *       if currentPlayer == configuration.players[0]:
   *           currentPlayer = configuration.players[1]
   *       else:
   *           currentPlayer = configuration.players[0]

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Decides the winner of the game after a successful move (or after a
   *   no-moves end-of-game state) according to the rules: no winner may
   *   be declared during the protection phase, a Knight leaving the
   *   central place wins, eliminating all opponent pieces wins, and when
   *   no moves are available the higher score wins (ties go to the
   *   current player).
   * Algorithm:
   *   numProt = configuration.numMovesProtection
   *   if game.numMoves < numProt:
   *       return null                       // protection phase forbids any winner
   *   // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
   *   central = configuration.centralPlace
   *   if lastPiece is Knight and
   *      lastMove.source == central and
   *      lastMove.destination != central:
   *       return lastPlayer
   *   // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
   *   counts = map from Player to count of pieces still on the board
   *   remaining = number of players in counts with count > 0
   *   if remaining == 1:
   *       return the unique player in counts with count > 0
   *   // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to
   *   // lastPlayer (i.e., the player who last acted / current player when
   *   // moves are exhausted).
   *   p0 = configuration.players[0]
   *   p1 = configuration.players[1]
   *   if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
   *   if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
   *   return lastPlayer                    // tie -> current/last player wins
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - used to count pieces by player.
   *   - configuration : Configuration - provides numMovesProtection,
   *                              centralPlace, and the list of players
   *                              (and their scores).
   *   - numMoves      : int - compared with numMovesProtection to gate
   *                          the protection phase.
   * Related Classes:
   *   Game, Player, Move, Place, Piece, Configuration, Knight
   * Input:
   *   - lastPlayer : Player - the player who just executed (or attempted)
   *                            the last move; used for the "Knight leaves
   *                            central" check and as the tie-breaker.
   *   - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved last; must be a
   *                            Knight to satisfy the central-exit win.
   *   - lastMove   : Move   - the move that was just executed; its
   *                            source/destination drive the central-exit
   *                            check.
   * Output:

   *               declared (still inside the protection phase, or none
   *               of the win conditions are met).
   * Pre-condition:

   *     configuration.players are populated.
   *   - game.numMoves is up to date (incremented after each successful
   *     move).

   *     successful move (or appropriate sentinels for the no-moves

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
   *   generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
   *   board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
   *   rule (global, protection, and piece-specific). The returned list is
   *   used by ConsolePlayer/RandomPlayer and by the win-condition check
   *   that detects "no available moves" situations.
   * Algorithm:
   *   result = empty list
   *   size = configuration.size
   *   for x in [0, size):
   *       for y in [0, size):
   *           piece = getPiece(x, y)
   *           if piece == null or piece.player != player:
   *               continue
   *           src = new Place(x, y)
   *           candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(game, src)
   *           for each move m in candidates:
   *               if not (VacantRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       NilMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OccupiedRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                   continue
   *               // piece-specific rules
   *               if piece is Knight:
   *                   if not (KnightMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                           KnightBlockRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                       continue
   *               elif piece is Archer:
   *                   if not ArcherMoveRule.validate(game, m):
   *                       continue
   *               // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
   *               result.add(m)
   *   return result
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - the 2D board queried for the player's pieces.

   *   KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
   * Input:

   *                      Must be one of configuration.players.
   * Output:

   *                  `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
   *                  holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
```

```java
public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
{
  int numProt = getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection();
  if (getNumMoves() < numProt)
    return null;
  
  // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
  Place central = getConfiguration().getCentralPlace();
  if (lastPiece instanceof Knight &&
      lastMove.getSource() == central &&
      lastMove.getDestination() != central)
  {
    return lastPlayer;
  }
  
  // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
  Piece[][] board = getBoard();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  java.util.Map<Player, Integer> counts = new java.util.HashMap<Player, Integer>();
  for (Player p : getConfiguration().getPlayers())
    counts.put(p, 0);
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece p = board[x][y];
      if (p != null && counts.containsKey(p.getPlayer()))
        counts.put(p.getPlayer(), counts.get(p.getPlayer()) + 1);
    }
  }
  Player remainingPlayer = null;
  int remaining = 0;
  for (java.util.Map.Entry<Player, Integer> entry : counts.entrySet())
  {
    if (entry.getValue() > 0)
    {
      remaining++;
      remainingPlayer = entry.getKey();
    }
  }
  if (remaining == 1)
    return remainingPlayer;
  
  // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to lastPlayer
  Player p0 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0);
  Player p1 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1);
  if (p0.getScore() > p1.getScore()) return p0;
  if (p1.getScore() > p0.getScore()) return p1;
  return lastPlayer;
}
```

```java
public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
{
  EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece piece = getPiece(x, y);
      if (piece == null || piece.getPlayer() != player)
        continue;
      Place src = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
      src.setX(x);
      src.setY(y);
      EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, src);
      for (Move m : candidates)
      {
        if (!(VacantRule.validate(this, m) &&
              NilMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OccupiedRule.validate(this, m) &&
              FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, m)))
          continue;
        if (piece instanceof Knight)
        {
          if (!(KnightMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
                KnightBlockRule.validate(this, m)))
            continue;
        }
        else if (piece instanceof Archer)
        {
          if (!ArcherMoveRule.validate(this, m))
            continue;
        }
        result.add(m);
      }
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
public void movePiece(final Move move)
{
  Piece piece = getPiece(move.getSource());
  getBoard()[move.getDestination().getX()][move.getDestination().getY()] = piece;
  getBoard()[move.getSource().getX()][move.getSource().getY()] = null;
}
```

For `updateScore`:
```java
public void updateScore(final Player player, final Piece piece, final Move move)
{
  int dx = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getX() - move.getSource().getX());
  int dy = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getY() - move.getSource().getY());
  player.setScore(player.getScore() + dx + dy);
}
```

```java
package edu.pa20;

import edu.pa20.util.Pa20AdapterFactory;
import org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList;
import org.eclipse.emf.common.util.EList;
import org.eclipse.emf.ecore.EClass;

public class JesonMor extends Game
{
  // ... constructor, eStaticClass omitted
  
  public Player start()
  {
    // initial setup
    setCurrentPlayer(getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0));
    setNumMoves(0);
    refreshOutput();
    while (true)
    {
      EList<Move> availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(getCurrentPlayer());
      if (availableMoves.isEmpty())
      {
        // no-moves end-of-game: higher score wins, ties to currentPlayer
        Player p0 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0);
        Player p1 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1);
        if (p0.getScore() > p1.getScore()) return p0;
        if (p1.getScore() > p0.getScore()) return p1;
```

```java
public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
{
  int numProt = getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection();
  if (getNumMoves() < numProt)
    return null;
  
  // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
  Place central = getConfiguration().getCentralPlace();
  if (lastPiece instanceof Knight &&
      lastMove.getSource() == central &&
      lastMove.getDestination() != central)
  {
    return lastPlayer;
  }
  
  // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
  Piece[][] board = getBoard();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  java.util.Map<Player, Integer> counts = new java.util.HashMap<Player, Integer>();
  for (Player p : getConfiguration().getPlayers())
    counts.put(p, 0);
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece p = board[x][y];
      if (p != null && counts.containsKey(p.getPlayer()))
        counts.put(p.getPlayer(), counts.get(p.getPlayer()) + 1);
    }
  }
  Player remainingPlayer = null;
  int remaining = 0;
  for (java.util.Map.Entry<Player, Integer> entry : counts.entrySet())
  {
    if (entry.getValue() > 0)
    {
      remaining++;
      remainingPlayer = entry.getKey();
    }
  }
  if (remaining == 1)
    return remainingPlayer;
  
  // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to lastPlayer
  Player p0 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0);
  Player p1 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1);
  if (p0.getScore() > p1.getScore()) return p0;
  if (p1.getScore() > p0.getScore()) return p1;
  return lastPlayer;
}
```

```java
public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
{
  EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece piece = getPiece(x, y);
      if (piece == null || piece.getPlayer() != player)
        continue;
      Place src = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
      src.setX(x);
      src.setY(y);
      EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, src);
      for (Move m : candidates)
      {
        if (!(VacantRule.validate(this, m) &&
              NilMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OccupiedRule.validate(this, m) &&
              FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, m)))
          continue;
        if (piece instanceof Knight)
        {
          if (!(KnightMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
                KnightBlockRule.validate(this, m)))
            continue;
        }
        else if (piece instanceof Archer)
        {
          if (!ArcherMoveRule.validate(this, m))
            continue;
        }
        result.add(m);
      }
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
public void movePiece(final Move move)
{
  Piece piece = getPiece(move.getSource());
  getBoard()[move.getDestination().getX()][move.getDestination().getY()] = piece;
  getBoard()[move.getSource().getX()][move.getSource().getY()] = null;
}
```

For `updateScore`:
```java
public void updateScore(final Player player, final Piece piece, final Move move)
{
  int dx = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getX() - move.getSource().getX());
  int dy = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getY() - move.getSource().getY());
  player.setScore(player.getScore() + dx + dy);
}
```

```java
   *   if game.numMoves < numProt:
   *       return null                       // protection phase forbids any winner
   *   // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
   *   central = configuration.centralPlace
   *   if lastPiece is Knight and
   *      lastMove.source == central and
   *      lastMove.destination != central:
   *       return lastPlayer
   *   // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
   *   counts = map from Player to count of pieces still on the board
   *   remaining = number of players in counts with count > 0
   *   if remaining == 1:
   *       return the unique player in counts with count > 0
   *   // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to
   *   // lastPlayer (i.e., the player who last acted / current player when
   *   // moves are exhausted).
   *   p0 = configuration.players[0]
   *   p1 = configuration.players[1]
   *   if p0.score > p1.score: return p0
   *   if p1.score > p0.score: return p1
   *   return lastPlayer                    // tie -> current/last player wins
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - used to count pieces by player.
   *   - configuration : Configuration - provides numMovesProtection,
   *                              centralPlace, and the list of players
   *                              (and their scores).
   *   - numMoves      : int - compared with numMovesProtection to gate
   *                          the protection phase.
   * Related Classes:
   *   Game, Player, Move, Place, Piece, Configuration, Knight
   * Input:
   *   - lastPlayer : Player - the player who just executed (or attempted)
   *                            the last move; used for the "Knight leaves
   *                            central" check and as the tie-breaker.
   *   - lastPiece  : Piece  - the piece that was moved last; must be a
   *                            Knight to satisfy the central-exit win.
   *   - lastMove   : Move   - the move that was just executed; its
   *                            source/destination drive the central-exit
   *                            check.
   * Output:
   *   - Player  - the winning player, or null if no winner can yet be
   *               declared (still inside the protection phase, or none
   *               of the win conditions are met).
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - configuration is initialized; configuration.centralPlace and
   *     configuration.players are populated.
   *   - game.numMoves is up to date (incremented after each successful
   *     move).
   *   - lastPlayer, lastPiece, and lastMove describe the most recent
   *     successful move (or appropriate sentinels for the no-moves
   *     case handled by the caller).
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The board, scores, and numMoves are not modified.
   *   - Returns null when the game continues, or a non-null Player
   *     indicating the winner.

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Computes the complete list of legal moves for a given player by
   *   generating candidate moves from every piece of that player on the
   *   board and then filtering the candidates through every applicable
   *   rule (global, protection, and piece-specific). The returned list is
   *   used by ConsolePlayer/RandomPlayer and by the win-condition check
   *   that detects "no available moves" situations.
   * Algorithm:
   *   result = empty list
   *   size = configuration.size
   *   for x in [0, size):
   *       for y in [0, size):
   *           piece = getPiece(x, y)
   *           if piece == null or piece.player != player:
   *               continue
   *           src = new Place(x, y)
   *           candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(game, src)
   *           for each move m in candidates:
   *               if not (VacantRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       NilMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       OccupiedRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                       FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                   continue
   *               // piece-specific rules
   *               if piece is Knight:
   *                   if not (KnightMoveRule.validate(game, m) and
   *                           KnightBlockRule.validate(game, m)):
   *                       continue
   *               elif piece is Archer:
   *                   if not ArcherMoveRule.validate(game, m):
   *                       continue
   *               // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
   *               result.add(m)
   *   return result
   * Related Features:
   *   - board         : PieceArray2D - the 2D board queried for the player's pieces.
   *   - configuration : Configuration - provides the board size.
   *   - currentPlayer : Player - the player whose turn it is (used for
   *                              context; the method is parameterized by

   *   NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule,
   *   KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
   * Input:

   *                      Must be one of configuration.players.
   * Output:

   *                  `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
   *                  holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
   *                  that satisfies every applicable validation rule.
   * Pre-condition:

   *     integer; configuration.players contains `player`.
```

```java
      if (winner != null)

      // switch player
      if (getCurrentPlayer() == getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0))
        setCurrentPlayer(getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1));
      else
        setCurrentPlayer(getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0));
    }
  }
```

```java
public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
{
  int numProt = getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection();
  if (getNumMoves() < numProt)
    return null;
  
  // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
  Place central = getConfiguration().getCentralPlace();
  if (lastPiece instanceof Knight &&
      lastMove.getSource() == central &&
      lastMove.getDestination() != central)
  {
    return lastPlayer;
  }
  
  // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
  Piece[][] board = getBoard();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  java.util.Map<Player, Integer> counts = new java.util.HashMap<Player, Integer>();
  for (Player p : getConfiguration().getPlayers())
    counts.put(p, 0);
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece p = board[x][y];
      if (p != null && counts.containsKey(p.getPlayer()))
        counts.put(p.getPlayer(), counts.get(p.getPlayer()) + 1);
    }
  }
  Player remainingPlayer = null;
  int remaining = 0;
  for (java.util.Map.Entry<Player, Integer> entry : counts.entrySet())
  {
    if (entry.getValue() > 0)
    {
      remaining++;
      remainingPlayer = entry.getKey();
    }
  }
  if (remaining == 1)
    return remainingPlayer;
  
  // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to lastPlayer
  Player p0 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0);
  Player p1 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1);
  if (p0.getScore() > p1.getScore()) return p0;
  if (p1.getScore() > p0.getScore()) return p1;
  return lastPlayer;
}
```

Wait, I should use `BasicEList` for EList, but here I'm using `java.util.Map` which is fine. For the EList return type in `getAvailableMoves`, I should use `BasicEList`.

```java
public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
{
  EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
  int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
  for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
  {
    for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
    {
      Piece piece = getPiece(x, y);
      if (piece == null || piece.getPlayer() != player)
        continue;
      Place src = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
      src.setX(x);
      src.setY(y);
      EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, src);
      for (Move m : candidates)
      {
        if (!(VacantRule.validate(this, m) &&
              NilMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, m) &&
              OccupiedRule.validate(this, m) &&
              FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, m)))
          continue;
        if (piece instanceof Knight)
        {
          if (!(KnightMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
                KnightBlockRule.validate(this, m)))
            continue;
        }
        else if (piece instanceof Archer)
        {
          if (!ArcherMoveRule.validate(this, m))
            continue;
        }
        result.add(m);
      }
    }
  }
  return result;
}
```

```java
public void movePiece(final Move move)
{
  Piece piece = getPiece(move.getSource());
  getBoard()[move.getDestination().getX()][move.getDestination().getY()] = piece;
  getBoard()[move.getSource().getX()][move.getSource().getY()] = null;
}
```

For `updateScore`:
```java
public void updateScore(final Player player, final Piece piece, final Move move)
{
  int dx = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getX() - move.getSource().getX());
  int dy = Math.abs(move.getDestination().getY() - move.getSource().getY());
  player.setScore(player.getScore() + dx + dy);
}
```

  public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
  {
    int numProt = getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection();
    if (getNumMoves() < numProt)
      return null;                       // protection phase forbids any winner

    // Win condition 1: a Knight leaves the central square
    Place central = getConfiguration().getCentralPlace();
    if (lastPiece instanceof Knight &&
        lastMove.getSource() == central &&
        lastMove.getDestination() != central)
    {
      return lastPlayer;
    }

    // Win condition 2: only one player's pieces remain
    Map<Player, Integer> counts = new HashMap<Player, Integer>();
    for (Player p : getConfiguration().getPlayers())
      counts.put(p, 0);
    Piece[][] board = getBoard();
    int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
    for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
    {
      for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
      {
        Piece p = board[x][y];
        if (p != null && counts.containsKey(p.getPlayer()))
          counts.put(p.getPlayer(), counts.get(p.getPlayer()) + 1);
      }
    }
    Player remainingPlayer = null;
    int remaining = 0;
    for (Map.Entry<Player, Integer> entry : counts.entrySet())
    {
      if (entry.getValue() > 0)
      {
        remaining++;
        remainingPlayer = entry.getKey();
      }
    }
    if (remaining == 1)
      return remainingPlayer;

    // End-of-game by no available moves: higher score wins, ties to lastPlayer
    Player p0 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(0);
    Player p1 = getConfiguration().getPlayers().get(1);
    if (p0.getScore() > p1.getScore()) return p0;
    if (p1.getScore() > p0.getScore()) return p1;
    return lastPlayer;                    // tie -> current/last player wins

   * Related Classes:
   *   Game, Player, Piece, Move, Place, Configuration, Rule, VacantRule,
   *   NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, FirstNMovesProtectionRule,
   *   KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule, ArcherMoveRule, Knight, Archer
   * Input:
   *   - player : Player - the player whose legal moves are being enumerated.
   *                      Must be one of configuration.players.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - the set of all legal moves currently available to
   *                  `player`. May be empty. Each Move has a source that
   *                  holds one of the player's pieces and a destination
   *                  that satisfies every applicable validation rule.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - configuration is set and configuration.size is a positive odd
   *     integer; configuration.players contains `player`.
   *   - The board has been initialized consistent with configuration.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The returned list contains exactly the moves that would pass the
   *     full rule pipeline for the current board and game state.
   *   - No mutation of the board, scores, or numMoves occurs.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
  {
    EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
    int size = getConfiguration().getSize();
    for (int x = 0; x < size; x++)
    {
      for (int y = 0; y < size; y++)
      {
        Piece piece = getPiece(x, y);
        if (piece == null || piece.getPlayer() != player)
          continue;
        Place src = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
        src.setX(x);
        src.setY(y);
        EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, src);
        for (Move m : candidates)
        {
          if (!(VacantRule.validate(this, m) &&
                NilMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
                OutOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, m) &&
                OccupiedRule.validate(this, m) &&
                FirstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, m)))
            continue;
          // piece-specific rules
          if (piece instanceof Knight)
          {
            if (!(KnightMoveRule.validate(this, m) &&
                  KnightBlockRule.validate(this, m)))
              continue;
          }
          else if (piece instanceof Archer)
          {
            if (!ArcherMoveRule.validate(this, m))
              continue;
          }
          // other piece types: not subject to piece-specific rules
          result.add(m);
        }
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

} // JesonMor

```java
   *   Generates all structurally-valid candidate moves for a Knight piece
   *   at the given source square. A Knight moves in an L-shape: two
   *   squares along one axis combined with one square along the
   *   orthogonal axis, giving up to eight destinations. Only destinations
   *   that lie within the board are emitted; the caller still applies the
   *   global rules (boundary, occupation, ...) and the Knight-specific

   *   candidates = empty list
   *   offsets = [(2,1), (2,-1), (-2,1), (-2,-1),

   *   size = game.configuration.size
   *   for each (dx, dy) in offsets:
   *       nx = source.x + dx
   *       ny = source.y + dy
   *       if 0 <= nx < size and 0 <= ny < size:
   *           candidates.add(new Move(source, new Place(nx, ny)))
   *   return candidates

   *   baked into the algorithm).
```

```java
   *   travel two squares along one axis and one square along the
   *   orthogonal axis (i.e., an L-shape). It does not check boundary,
   *   occupancy, or the blocking square; those are handled by other
   *   rules.

   *   dst = move.destination

   *   dy = abs(dst.y - src.y)
   *   return (dx == 2 and dy == 1) or (dx == 1 and dy == 2)
   * Related Features:
   *   None (KnightMoveRule has no attributes; the rule is purely a
   *   shape check on the supplied move).

   *   Game, Move, Place

   *                   rule, kept for the Rule interface).
   *   - move  : Move - the candidate move whose displacement is
   *                     checked.
   * Output:
   *   - boolean  - true if the move displacement is exactly an L-shape;
   *                false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The board, scores, and move object are not modified.
   *   - The result is true for L-shaped moves and false for any other
   *     displacement.
```

```java
   *   None (KnightMoveRule has no attributes; the rule is purely a
   *   shape check on the supplied move).

   *                   rule, kept for the Rule interface).
   *   - move  : Move - the candidate move whose displacement is
   *                     checked.
   * Output:
   *   - boolean  - true if the move displacement is exactly an L-shape;

   *   - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
```

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   *   Validates the geometric shape of a Knight move: the move must
   *   travel two squares along one axis and one square along the
   *   orthogonal axis (i.e., an L-shape). It does not check boundary,
   *   occupancy, or the blocking square; those are handled by other
   *   rules.
   * Algorithm:
   *   src = move.source
   *   dst = move.destination
   *   dx = abs(dst.x - src.x)
   *   dy = abs(dst.y - src.y)
   *   return (dx == 2 and dy == 1) or (dx == 1 and dy == 2)
   * Related Features:
   *   None (KnightMoveRule has no attributes; the rule is purely a
   *   shape check on the supplied move).
   * Related Classes:
   *   Game, Move, Place
   * Input:
   *   - game : Game - the current game state (not consulted by this
   *                   rule, kept for the Rule interface).
   *   - move  : Move - the candidate move whose displacement is
   *                     checked.
   * Output:
   *   - boolean  - true if the move displacement is exactly an L-shape;
   *                false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - move.source and move.destination are non-null Places.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The board, scores, and move object are not modified.
   *   - The result is true for L-shaped moves and false for any other
   *     displacement.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    final Place src = move.getSource();
    final Place dst = move.getDestination();
    final int dx = Math.abs(dst.getX() - src.getX());
    final int dy = Math.abs(dst.getY() - src.getY());
    return (dx == 2 && dy == 1) || (dx == 1 && dy == 2);
  }

```java
   * The algorithm correctly computes the blocking square per the requirement:
   *   - 2x1 L-shape: block at ((src.x+dst.x)/2, src.y)
   *   - 1x2 L-shape: block at (src.x, (src.y+dst.y)/2)
   * The rule returns false if any piece (friend or foe) occupies the leg square,
   * matching the requirement that "the move is invalid if any piece occupies this
   * intermediate square." The behavior of deferring (returning true) for non-L-shapes
   * is a valid design choice that cleanly separates geometry (KnightMoveRule) from
```

    Place dst = move.getDestination();
    int dx = dst.getX() - src.getX();
    int dy = dst.getY() - src.getY();
    int absDx = Math.abs(dx);
    int absDy = Math.abs(dy);
    int legX = src.getX();
    int legY = src.getY();
    if (absDx == 2 && absDy == 1)
    {
      legX = (src.getX() + dst.getX()) / 2;
      legY = src.getY();
    }

    {
      legX = src.getX();
      legY = (src.getY() + dst.getY()) / 2;
    }
    else
    {
      // Not a knight L-shape; defer to other rules.
      return true;
    }

```java
   *   Validates that a candidate move is a legal Archer move: the move must
   *   travel along a single orthogonal axis, and either the path between
   *   source and destination must be completely clear (non-capturing) or
   *   there must be exactly one piece of any color acting as a "screen"
```
